title: Historic Feat: SpaceX Catches Starship Midair Following 22-Hour Orbital Voyage
snippet: SpaceX successfully caught its Starship spacecraft with giant launch tower arms following a 22-hour orbital flight, achieving a major landmark despite losing its first-stage booster shortly after launch.
content:
CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — In a spectacle straight out of science fiction, SpaceX successfully snagged its massive Starship spacecraft out of the sky on Saturday, concluding a dramatic 22-hour orbital mission. The spacecraft safely returned to its Texas launch pad, guided delicately into the giant mechanical arms of its launch tower.

The landmark capture represents a major leap forward for chief executive Elon Musk’s dream of fully reusable space hardware. However, the mission fell short of a total victory after the rocket's Super Heavy first-stage booster suffered an engine anomaly and exploded over the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Friday's liftoff.

A Triumph Amid Booster Troubles

Despite missing out on a planned 'double catch,' the flawless recovery of the upper-stage spacecraft stole the show. Supported high above the ground by the launch tower’s mechanical arms, the stainless-steel vehicle sustained minimal visible damage. Heat shields and guidance systems performed as expected throughout its high-speed reentry and descent.

SpaceX commentators erupted with excitement during the live broadcast as the craft settled into the tower. 'Look at her! Baby, she’s back!' shouted SpaceX commentator Dan Huot.

During its nearly day-long trek, Starship completed 14 orbits at an altitude of 165 miles (265 kilometers) and successfully deployed 26 next-generation Starlink internet satellites. It marked the 15th flight of a full-scale Starship and only its second successful orbital trip.

Paving the Way for Artemis and Mars

The achievement drew high praise from NASA leadership, which is investing billions into Starship to serve as the human landing system for upcoming Artemis moon missions. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman commended the feat on X, describing the maneuver as 'almost magic' and noting it brings humanity one step closer to returning to the lunar surface.

Engineers are currently analyzing telemetry from the lost booster, which automatically initiated a self-destruct sequence over the ocean after its guidance system detected an off-nominal flight path. Meanwhile, SpaceX is preparing to shift upcoming Starship operations toward NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida as it prepares for deep-space missions.
